akhfash:11-11.t: He said ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ إِن كَانَ عَلَىٰ ٱلْهُدَىٰ﴾, then He said ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ إِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ﴾: He made it a badal (substitute) for it, and made the khabar (predicate) ﴿أَلَمْ يَعْلَم بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرَىٰ﴾.

akhfash:17-18.t: And He said ﴿فَلْيَدْعُ نَادِيَهُ﴾ ﴿سَنَدْعُ ٱلزَّبَانِيَةَ﴾: ﴿نادِيَهُ﴾ here is his clan, for they are the people of the nādī (assembly), and the nādī is his place and his gathering. As for ﴿الزّبانِيَةُ﴾, some said its singular is "الزَبانِي", and some said "الزَابِن" — I heard "الزابِن" from ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar — and some said "الزِبْنِية". The Arabs hardly know this, and make it one of the plurals that have no singular, like "أَبابِيل": you say "جاءَتْ إِبِلِي أبابِيل" ("my camels came in flocks"), that is: in separate groups. This comes in the meaning of multiplicity, like "عَباديِد" and "شَعارِير".

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿اقْرَأْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿بِاسْمِ﴾: the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and ﴿اسم﴾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿الَّذِي﴾: naʿt (adjective) of ربك; ﴿خَلَقَ﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), and the clause اقرأ… is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿خَلَقَ﴾: badal (substitute) for the preceding one, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir); ﴿الْإِنْسانَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿مِنْ عَلَقٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿اقْرَأْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause emphasizes the preceding one; ﴿وَ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿وَرَبُّكَ الْأَكْرَمُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a second naʿt (adjective) of ربك; ﴿عَلَّمَ﴾: a past verb, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿بِالْقَلَمِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the verbal clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿عَلَّمَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and it is a badal (substitute) for the preceding one; ﴿الْإِنْسانَ﴾: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿ما﴾: second direct object; ﴿لَمْ يَعْلَمْ﴾: an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke; ﴿إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿لَيَطْغى﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿أَنْ رَآهُ﴾: an is a maṣdar-forming particle that puts the verb in the accusative, and a past verb and its first object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); ﴿اسْتَغْنى﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent; the clause is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿إِنَّ﴾: a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters); ﴿إِلى رَبِّكَ﴾: the fronted khabar (predicate) of inna; ﴿الرُّجْعى﴾: its postponed noun; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ﴾: the hamza is an interrogative particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿الَّذِي﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿يَنْهى﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿عَبْداً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿صَلَّى﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ﴾: the hamza is an interrogative particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿إِنْ﴾: a conditional particle that puts the verb in the jussive; ﴿كانَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its noun latent (mustatir); ﴿عَلَى الْهُدى﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of kāna; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿أَوْ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿أَمَرَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿بِالتَّقْوى﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ﴾: the hamza is an interrogative particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿إِنْ﴾: a conditional particle that puts the verb in the jussive; ﴿كَذَّبَ﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); ﴿وَتَوَلَّى﴾: conjoined to كذب; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿أَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ﴾: ألم: the hamza is a particle of interrogation and affirmation (taqrīr), and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam; ﴿بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾: the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and anna and its noun; ﴿يَرى﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from anna and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of يعلم.

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke; ﴿لَئِنْ﴾: the lām is the one that prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam), and إن is a conditional particle that puts the verb in the jussive; ﴿لَمْ يَنْتَهِ﴾: an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; ﴿لَنَسْفَعاً﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the light nūn of emphasis, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿بِالنَّاصِيَةِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position, and the clause لم ينته is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿ناصِيَةٍ﴾: badal (substitute) for الناصية; ﴿كاذِبَةٍ خاطِئَةٍ﴾: two adjectives (naʿt).

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿فَلْيَدْعُ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition), and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿نادِيَهُ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿سَنَدْعُ﴾: the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the wāw, which is dropped in recitation; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿الزَّبانِيَةَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke; ﴿لا تُطِعْهُ﴾: an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā; the hāʾ is its object and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَاسْجُدْ﴾: an imperative verb whose agent is latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَاقْتَرِبْ﴾: conjoined to اسجد.

farraa:1-1.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ﴾.
This is the first of the Qur'an that was revealed to the Prophet, may Allah bless him.

farraa:2-2.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿خَلَقَ ٱلإِنسَانَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ﴾.
It was said «من علق», whereas it is [one] «علقةٌ» (clot), because «الإنسان» has a plural meaning; so «العلق» was taken as plural, to match the verse-endings.

farraa:7-7.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَن رَّآهُ ٱسْتَغْنَىٰ﴾.
He did not say: أن رأى نفسه (that he saw himself). When the Arabs make a verb that is satisfied with one noun [i.e. a verb with a single object] fall upon themselves, or make it fall from someone else upon himself, they put «نفس» in the place of the pronoun. So they say: قتلتَ نفسك (you killed yourself), and they do not say: قتلتَك or قتلته [for the same person]; and they say: قتل نفسَه (he killed himself) and قتلتُ نفسى (I killed myself). But when the verb requires a noun and a predicate (khabar), they drop «النفس» and say: متى تراك خارجاً (when do you consider yourself going out?) and متى نظنك خارجاً (when do we think you are going out?). [Translator's note: «نظنك» is as printed; the parallel with «تراك» suggests «تظنك» (when do you think yourself …).] And His word, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿أَن رَّآهُ ٱسْتَغْنَىٰ﴾, is of this kind.

farraa:9-10.t:
His words, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ ٱلَّذِي يَنْهَىٰ (9) عَبْداً إِذَا صَلَّىٰ﴾.
It was revealed concerning Abū Jahl: he used to come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at his place of prayer, and harm him and forbid him; so Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ ٱلَّذِي يَنْهَىٰ عَبْداً إِذَا صَلَّىٰ﴾?, meaning the Prophet ﷺ.

farraa:13-13.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ إِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ﴾.
There is an Arabic [construction] in it. Its like in ordinary speech would be if it were said: أرأيت الذى ينهى عبداً إذا صلّى وهو كاذب متولٍّ عن الذكر؟ (Have you seen the one who forbids a servant when he prays, while he is lying and turning away from the Reminder?), i.e.: what could be more astonishing than this?

farraa:14-14.t:
Then He said — woe to him! — ﴿أَلَمْ يَعْلَم بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرَىٰ﴾.
Meaning Abū Jahl. Then He said: ﴿كَلاَّ لَئِن لَّمْ يَنتَهِ لَنَسْفَعاً بِٱلنَّاصِيَةِ﴾.
His forelock (ناصيته): the front of his head; i.e.: We shall surely bend it down, We shall surely seize it, We shall surely abase him and humiliate him. It is also said: We shall surely drag [him] by the forelock to the Fire, as He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿فَيُؤْخَذُ بِالنَّواصِى والأَقْدَامِ﴾, and they are thrown into the Fire. It is also said: We shall surely blacken his face; so the forelock stood in for the face, because it is at the front of the face.

farraa:15-16.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَنَسْفَعاً بِٱلنَّاصِيَةِ نَاصِيَةٍ﴾.
By repetition (takrīr, i.e. badal (substitute)), as He said: ﴿إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ، صِرَاطِ اللهِ﴾. The definite is made to follow the indefinite by repetition, and the indefinite the definite. Whoever puts (ناصيةً) in the accusative makes it an act of the definite [Translator's note: so the source, «جعله فعلا للمعرفة»; the sense appears to be that the accusative is governed with reference to the definite «الناصية», e.g. as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the wording may be corrupt], and it is permissible in reading.

farraa:17-18.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلْيَدْعُ نَادِيَهُ سَنَدْعُ ٱلزَّبَانِيَةَ﴾.
They are stronger, and they work with hands and feet; and the she-camel تزْبِن (pushes off) the milker and kicks him with her foot.
Al-Kisāʾī said, later in life: the singular of «الزبانية» is زِبْنِىٌّ; before that he used to say: I have not heard a singular for it. And I do not know whether it was by analogy (qiyās) on his part or by hearing (samāʿ). In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is: "كَلاَّ لئِن لَّمْ يَنْتَهِ لأسْفَعاً بِالنَّاصِيَةِ", and in it also: "فَلْيَدْعُ إلىّ نَادِيَه فَسَأَدْعُو الزَّبَانِيَة".

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-ʿAlaq
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ﴾ ("recite in the name of your Lord Who created"): it has come in the exegesis that the first verse of the Qur'an to be revealed was ﴿اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ﴾.

zajjaj:4-4.t: And His saying: ﴿الَّذِي عَلَّمَ بِالقَلَمِ﴾ ("Who taught by the pen"): that is, Who taught writing.

zajjaj:6-7.t: And His saying: ﴿كَلا إنَّ الإنْسانَ لَيَطْغى﴾ ﴿أنْ رَآهُ اسْتَغْنى﴾ ("nay, the human being surely transgresses, because he sees himself self-sufficient"): this was revealed about Abū Jahl ibn Hishām; and likewise ﴿أرَأيْتَ الَّذِي يَنْهى﴾ [al-ʿAlaq: 9] ﴿عَبْدًا إذا صَلّى﴾ [al-ʿAlaq: 10] ("have you seen the one who forbids a servant when he prays?"), because Abū Jahl said: "If I see Muhammad praying, I will tread on his neck."

zajjaj:15-15.t: And His saying: ﴿كَلا لَئِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهِ لَنَسْفَعًا بِالنّاصِيَةِ﴾ ("nay, if he does not desist, We will surely seize him by the forelock"): that is, We will surely drag his forelock to the Fire. One says ”سَفَعْتُ بِالشَّيْءِ“ when I have grasped something and pulled it violently.

zajjaj:16-16.t: And His saying: ﴿ناصِيَةٍ كاذِبَةٍ خاطِئَةٍ﴾ ("a lying, sinning forelock"): its interpretation is "by a forelock whose owner is lying and sinning", just as one says ”فُلانٌ نَهارُهُ صائِمٌ، ولَيْلُهُ قائِمٌ“ ("so-and-so, his day is fasting and his night is standing in prayer"), the meaning being "he fasts in his day and stands in prayer in his night".

zajjaj:17-17.t: ﴿فَلْيَدْعُ نادِيَهُ﴾ ("then let him call his assembly"): its meaning is: let him call the people of his assembly, i.e. the people of his gathering, who were his clan; that is, let him seek their help.

zajjaj:18-18.t: ﴿سَنَدْعُ الزَّبانِيَةَ﴾ ("We will call the zabāniya"): ”اَلزَّبانِيَةُ“ are the harsh and severe ones; their singular is ”زِبْنِيَةٌ“. Here they are the angels; Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قُوا أنْفُسَكم وأهْلِيكم نارًا وقُودُها النّاسُ والحِجارَةُ عَلَيْها مَلائِكَةٌ غِلاظٌ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 6] ("O you who believe, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are harsh angels"), and they are the zabāniya.

zajjaj:19-19.t: ﴿كَلا﴾: that is, the matter is not as Abū Jahl holds. ﴿لا تُطِعْهُ واسْجُدْ واقْتَرِبْ﴾ ("do not obey him; prostrate and draw near"): that is, and draw near to your Lord through obedience.
